## Ctx.renderBroadcastMedia() method

Sends a media message to multiple users in bulk.

**Signature:**

```typescript
renderBroadcastMedia(ids: number[], languageCode: string[], keyboard?: ITInBoKb | null, data?: ITData | null, AGBaseId?: string | null, options?: ITOptReplyPhoto | ITOptReplyVideo | ITOptReplyAudio | ITOptReplyDocument | ITOptReplyAnimation | ITOptReplyVoice | ITOptReplyVideoNote | ITOptReplySticker | ITOptReplyLocation | ITOptReplyContact | null, throwError?: boolean | null, chunkSize?: number | null, chunkDelayMs?: number | null, excludeIds?: number[] | null, onProgress?: ((done: number, total: number) => void | Promise<void>) | null, startFrom?: number | null, concurrency?: number | null): Promise<{
        successCount: number;
        failedCount: number;
        totalCount: number;
        skippedCount: number;
        retryable: Array<{
            index: number;
            id: number;
            error: unknown;
        }>;
    }>;
```

## Remarks

Media type and arg are inferred from the template `<g-media>` block. If a supported media type (`photo`<!-- -->, `video`<!-- -->, `audio`<!-- -->, `document`<!-- -->) uses a pipe-delimited `src`<!-- -->, it is sent as a Telegram media group. Telegram media groups do not support reply markup, so keyboards are ignored for grouped media. Automatically throttles after 30 messages to respect Telegram rate limits. Uses each user's specified language code for template rendering. Fail-fast validation runs for every recipient media BEFORE the loop (programmer errors always throw, never fall back). Per-recipient send failures follow `Ctx.classifySendError`<!-- -->: `retryable` errors are counted and the loop continues; `fallback-text` errors additionally trigger a best-effort fallback-text send to that recipient (nested failures ignored). `failedCount`<!-- -->/`firstError` semantics are preserved either way; loop structure and pacing are untouched. Retryable failures (`429`<!-- -->/`5xx`<!-- -->/network) never abort the run: they are recorded in `retryable` (absolute `index` + `id` + `error`<!-- -->, completion order) while the checkpoint keeps advancing, so callers can re-drive just those entries with a fresh pass. `firstError` stays the first failure of any kind. Checkpoint-first (anti-spam over speed): `startFrom` resumes after a restart without resending (indexes below count as skipped, `done` in `onProgress` counts processed recipients, `total` is `ids.length`<!-- -->); `concurrency` defaults to `1` (sequential) and can be raised when throughput matters. Every resolved media input is cloned per recipient via `Ctx.cloneMediaInput`<!-- -->, so parallel workers never share one mutable `InputFile` instance.

## Example


```typescript
async handleCallbackQueryData() {
  const userIds = [123456, 789012]
  const langs = [`en`, `id`]
  await this.renderBroadcastMedia(userIds, langs)
}
```
